correctness.rationale: For crown graph Cr_n=K_n,n-M_n, constrained neighborhood sums are x_i+Y-y_i at a_i and y_i+X-x_i at b_i if their own label is 0 or 1. Synchronized x_i=y_i=z_i with sum_i z_i=3 gives a feasible weight-6 function. If total <6, a shore has weight <=2; at a zero coordinate the opposite lower bound forces a contradiction. At equality, the detailed 0,1,2 side-total case split excludes X<=2 and Y<=2 for n>=4; X=Y=3 then forces x_i=y_i on low coordinates and equality of totals forces the remaining high coordinate to agree. Thus precisely binom(n+2,3) optima. Independent exhaustive bounded-weight label searches yielded Cr_4:20, Cr_5:35, Cr_6:56, Cr_7:84, all synchronized; Cr_3 had 18 optima of which only 10 synchronized, confirming the excluded boundary. These finite checks are not the all-n proof.
